plan.planning_summary: This study tests four distinct strategy axes for a cold-mirror protective window: (1) classical quarter-wave Bragg stack with fixed pair count, (2) fully optimized non-quarter-wave thicknesses with the same layer count, (3) chirped stack with systematically graded thicknesses, and (4) reduced layer count to test manufacturing tolerance vs. performance trade-off. All routes use only HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica substrate, air incidence, targeting high transmission at 1000-1700 nm and high reflection at 300-450 nm. These axes are genuinely distinct because they test different physical approaches to band separation: periodic interference, numerical optimization, graded impedance matching, and layer-count sensitivity. Literature L21 directly motivates cold mirror design, L22 validates the HfO2/SiO2 material pair for optical coatings, L12 provides classical filter theory, and L29 supports modern optimization approaches.

routes.title: Classical Quarter-Wave Cold Mirror Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at the UV reflection band edge will achieve high UV reflection while maintaining adequate SWIR transmission, with performance saturating beyond a critical pair count.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength when optical thickness equals λ/4; placing the Bragg condition at ~450 nm creates a high-reflection band in 300-450 nm while allowing transmission at longer wavelengths where the stack becomes transparent.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_8 | sio2 substrate | 16 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count 16 is well below 30-layer limit
quarter-wave thicknesses are straightforward to deposit
HfO2/SiO2 pair has established deposition processes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector theory for band separation
Cold mirror design principles for IR transmission with visible/UV reflection
known_risks: Quarter-wave design may not optimize both bands simultaneously
May require more pairs to achieve target UV reflection
routes.execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_8 | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 16 layers. Optimize the quarter-wave reference wavelength and a uniform thickness scale factor to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.

routes.title: Chirped Stack with Graded Thickness
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses will broaden the UV reflection band and improve SWIR transmission compared to uniform quarter-wave stacks.
routes.design_principle: Chirped structures create multiple Bragg conditions across the stack, broadening the reflection band; grading thickness from substrate to air can improve impedance matching and reduce sideband reflection in the SWIR band.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_10 with linearly chirped thickness | sio2 substrate | 20 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped deposition requires calibrated thickness monitoring
Linear chirp is simpler to implement than arbitrary grading
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband reflection
Impedance matching through graded optical thickness
expected_advantages: Broader UV reflection band than quarter-wave stack
Potentially better SWIR transmission due to reduced sideband effects
Systematic design rule easier to manufacture than fully optimized stack
known_risks: Chirp parameters may not be optimal for this specific band combination
May require more layers to achieve same UV reflection as quarter-wave
Chirp direction (thick-to-thin vs thin-to-thick) affects performance
routes.execution_request_english: Design a chirped multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_10 with linearly chirped optical thickness from substrate to air | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 20 layers. Optimize starting thickness, ending thickness, chirp direction, and chirp rate to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.

routes.title: Reduced Layer Count for Manufacturing Tolerance
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A reduced layer count stack will achieve acceptable dual-band performance while improving manufacturing yield and reducing stress-related defects.
routes.design_principle: Fewer layers reduce cumulative stress, deposition time, and defect probability; if performance remains acceptable, the trade-off favors manufacturability for field-deployed cameras.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_5 | sio2 substrate | 10 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: 10 layers is well below 30-layer limit, reducing deposition time
Lower cumulative stress reduces delamination risk
Fewer interfaces reduce scatter and absorption losses
theory_basis: Layer count vs. performance trade-off in dielectric filters
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient UV reflection with only 10 layers
SWIR transmission may be compromised if UV reflection is inadequate
Performance ceiling lower than higher-count stacks

Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_5 | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 10 layers. Optimize the quarter-wave reference wavelength and a uniform thickness scale factor to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
